Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is issuing a final rule amending its Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process regulations. These regulations establish the process by which the public may file objections seeking administrative review of proposed projects and activities implementing land management plans on national forests and grasslands. The Department is amending these regulations to consolidate and streamline processes, increase efficiency, and better align with the Agency's statutory obligations and recent rescissions and revisions to National Environmental Policy Act regulations.

articles.title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery Management Plan; Fixed Gear Marking and Entanglement Risk Reduction
articles.summary: This rulemaking implements gear marking requirements and entanglement risk reduction measures for portions of the Pacific coast groundfish fishery. This rulemaking consists of mandatory requirements and voluntary measures. These new requirements and voluntary measures are established pursuant to the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act). The intent of the gear marking requirements is to increase the likelihood of attributing entanglements to a specific fishery and gear type. The intent of the risk reduction measures is to reduce bycatch by decreasing the likelihood of marine animal entanglements with fishing line.

articles.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine
articles.summary: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

articles.summary: We are advising the public that we have prepared a pest risk analysis that evaluates the risks associated with the importation of fresh passion fruit (Passiflora edulis) for consumption from Viet Nam into the United States. Based on the analysis, we have determined that the application of one or more designated phytosanitary measures will be sufficient to mitigate the risks of introducing or disseminating plant pests or noxious weeds via the importation of fresh passion fruit from Viet Nam into the United States. articles.content: China P&I seeks seat at global insurance top table - Splash247 China Shipowners Mutual Assurance Association, better known as China P&I Club, has formally applied to join the International Group of P&I Clubs, potentially bringing a mainland Chinese insurer into the powerful marine insurance grouping for the first time. The International Group confirmed it had received the application after China P&I chairman Xu Lirong and other senior executives visited its London headquarters on October 13. “The Group was pleased to welcome CPI Chairman Xu Li Rong and other senior members of CPI to the IG’s London office,” International Group chief executive Nick Shaw said.“ At the meeting, the IG was presented with CPI’s application to join the IG, which will be considered in accordance with the agreed process.” The application will be assessed over the coming months against admission criteria agreed by the existing clubs. The International Group stressed that the process will not affect the February 2027 P&I renewal. China P&I is not starting entirely outside the system. The Shanghai-headquartered mutual is already an approved reinsured association within the International Group structure and has reinsurance arrangements with several existing member clubs. Full membership, however, would represent a significant step up in its position in the international marine insurance market. articles.content: Tsakos returns to containership contracting in China - Splash247 Hengli Shipbuilding Greek shipping group Tsakos has returned to the containership newbuilding market, emerging behind an order for two 3,200 teu vessels at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries. The pair appear in the Athens-based owner’s latest fleet register, with both scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2028. Both will be scrubber-fitted and equipped with alternative maritime power systems, allowing them to connect to shore-side electricity while alongside. Shipping database records point to contracts signed in September, although Alphaliner said the exact timing remains unclear and that the orders could have been concluded in August or September. Market sources put the ships at around $48m each, depending on final specification, implying a combined investment of about $96m. Neither Tsakos nor Hengli has disclosed pricing. Charter arrangements are also unknown. Alphaliner noted that Tsakos has typically backed containership newbuildings with forward employment, but there is no indication yet whether the Hengli pair have already been fixed. The deal marks Tsakos’ first return to boxship contracting since 2022, when the group booked a series of approximately 2,800 teu vessels at HD Hyundai Mipo in South Korea. articles.content: Falklands offshore development faces new international legal challenge - Splash247 Falkland Islands Govt The dispute over offshore oil development around the Falkland Islands has escalated, with Argentina seeking emergency measures from an international maritime tribunal while the UK moves to protect companies involved in economic activity linked to the islands. Argentina filed a request with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), seeking provisional measures to prevent the UK from authorising hydrocarbon exploitation on the North Falkland Basin continental shelf. The filing forms part of an arbitration Buenos Aires launched against the UK under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Argentina argues that continued oil development could undermine its claimed sovereign rights and, while the dispute remains unresolved, risk serious harm to the marine environment. “The Argentine Republic reaffirms, once again, its legitimate and imprescriptible sovereign rights over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas. By history and by right: the Falkland Islands are Argentine,” the government said in its statement. London responded immediately with plans to use its Protection of Trading Interests legislation to shield UK companies and individuals from Argentine measures targeting activity around the Falklands. articles.content: Despite new record, Port of LA chief warns of tariff-driven planning risk - FreightWaves The Port of Los Angeles moved 1.42 million TEUs in September, its best single month ever and the highest monthly volume ever recorded by a port in the Western Hemisphere, Executive Director Gene Seroka said this week. He said lower tariff levels, resilient consumer demand, and cargo shifting away from constrained Panama Canal and Suez routes drove the surge. Record quarter September imports totaled 546,000 loaded TEUs, up 19% year over year and 26% above the port’s five-year average. Exports rose 10% to 126,000 loaded TEUs, while the port handled a record 371,000 empty containers as carriers repositioned equipment to Asia. July through September was the port’s strongest quarter on record at nearly 3 million TEUs, and June through September moved nearly 4 million containers. Through September, 2026 volume stood at nearly 8.1 million TEUs, up about 3% from the same period in 2025. Seroka said the port expects October volume of about 900,000 TEUs. He cited typhoon-related schedule disruptions in Asia, cargo “roll pools” before China’s national holiday, and continued holiday-season replenishment as reasons volumes should remain elevated. Trade and sourcing shifts Seroka in a media briefing said Vietnam is now the port’s second-largest trading partner behind China, while Thailand has entered the port’s top five for the first time. articles.content: Mexico truck exports soar 145% as US demand accelerates - FreightWaves Mexican manufacturers produced 15,181 heavy-duty vehicles during September, compared with 6,857 in the same month last year. Exports totaled 12,707 units, up 144.6% from September 2025, marking a significant acceleration in cross-border commercial vehicle shipments, according to figures from Mexico’s National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) presented by the National Association of Bus, Truck and Tractor-Trailer Producers (ANPACT). The September rebound comes as Mexico’s domestic heavy-duty vehicle market continues to struggle with weak sales, delayed fleet replacement decisions and uncertainty surrounding U.S. trade policies. Rogelio Arzate, executive president of ANPACT, said growing demand from U.S. customers preparing for new emissions standards has been a major factor behind the increase in production and exports. “The reason why production and exports are growing at the levels they are is precisely because the United States, our main trading partner, is currently undergoing this technology shift,” Arzate said during an October news conference. OK SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday reaffirmed South Korea's push to develop a new shipping route through the Arctic Ocean, saying it will be pursued in compliance with international norms and sanctions. The president made the pledge at a ceremony celebrating South Korea's successful voyage to Europe through the Arctic Ocean by a container ship, as the country seeks to operate summer-season container shipping services linking Asia and Europe. The PanStar Acro, a South Korean container ship, returned to the southeastern port city of Busan on Sunday after sailing via the Arctic Ocean north of Russia to Britain, the Netherlands and Poland, 50 days after leaving Busan. The pilot voyage marks the first successful trip by a South Korean container vessel via the Arctic Ocean, a route which is riskier due to polar ice, but offers faster shipping than routes via the Suez Canal. Growing international use of the Arctic route has, however, raised concerns that cooperation with Russian entities could undermine international sanctions imposed on Russia over its war with Ukraine. articles.content: Emarat Maritime piles six more tankers onto China orderbook - Splash247 Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry Dubai-based Emarat Maritime has added another six tanker newbuildings to its rapidly expanding fleet, lining up a series of 74,000 dwt LR1 product carriers in China. The company’s own fleet register now lists six LR1 newbuildings, with the first two scheduled for delivery in 2029 and the remaining four in 2030. Shipbuilding database records seen by Splash place the sextet at Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry. No contract price has emerged. Recent comparable Chinese LR1 orders have been running at around $55m per ship. Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend paid about $220m for four 74,000 dwt ships at Yangzijiang this summer, while Andriaki was linked to 73,500 dwt units at New Times at $55.1m each. On that basis, the Emarat sextet would benchmark at around $330m, although its actual contract terms remain undisclosed. The latest move significantly deepens Emarat’s exposure to the LR1 sector. Its operating fleet currently includes three older ships of roughly the same size — the 2007-built Dubai Diamond and Dubai Gold and the 2005-built Dubai Green. Delivery of the six new ships would therefore triple its LR1 fleet. The deal also takes Emarat’s overall newbuilding pipeline to 22 vessels. articles.content: Sweden frees sanctioned tanker after seven months - Splash247 Swedish Coast Guard Swedish authorities have cleared an EU-sanctioned product tanker to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor following an investigation into its registration and seaworthiness. The Swedish Transport Agency has lifted an operating ban on the 2007-built, 75,000 dwt Sea Owl I, after confirming that the vessel is now legitimately registered in Equatorial Guinea. The tanker had been detained off Trelleborg since March 12, when Swedish authorities boarded it over concerns about its flag status and documentation. The ship was originally claiming registration in Comoros, which authorities found to be invalid. A subsequent attempt to establish registration under the Cameroon flag also failed verification. The Swedish Transport Agency said it had now received confirmation directly from Equatorial Guinea and had reviewed the certificates and crew documentation required for the vessel to resume operations. The decision removes the Swedish operating prohibition, although the tanker remains subject to EU sanctions. Sweden’s coastguard stressed that the vessel was not suspected of breaching sanctions. Investigations involving two former masters, including allegations concerning false documentation, have been discontinued. articles.content: Prologis tops Q3 estimates, raises development starts forecast again - FreightWaves Logistics warehouse operator Prologis beat third-quarter expectations Thursday before the market opened, significantly raising its outlook for new developments. Prologis (NYSE: PLD) reported consolidated revenue of $2.39 billion for the quarter, reflecting an 8% year-over-year increase and topping consensus estimates by 8%. Core funds from operations (FFO) of $1.60 per share were 11 cents higher y/y and 3 cents better than analysts’ expectations. Lease signings in the period totaled 60 million square feet of space for the San Francisco-based real estate investment trust. Leases commenced totaled 55.9 million square feet, a 15% y/y decline. Average occupancy improved 30 basis points y/y to 95.1%, 10 bps higher than the in second quarter. Net effective rent change on Prologis’ portfolio of multiyear leases was 38%, near the company’s full-year goal of 40%. “Customers are running lean on inventory, and excess capacity within their networks has largely cleared,” said CEO Dan Letter. “We see healthy demand supported by e-commerce, advanced manufacturing and the build-out of the data center supply chain.” Table: Prologis’ key performance indicators The outlook for full-year 2026 core FFO was narrowed to a range of $6.25 to $6.29 per share, a 1-cent increase at the midpoint. articles.content: The Heavy-Duty Oil Standard Is Changing In January, What It Means For Your Fleet, Your Costs, And Your Equipment - FreightWaves If your trucks have been running the same heavy-duty diesel engine oil since roughly 2017, whether you manage a hundred-truck fleet, run a small operation of a few units, or own the one truck you drive yourself, that oil is about to be replaced by something new, because the American Petroleum Institute is rolling out a fresh engine oil category called PC-12 that takes effect at the start of January 2027, and everybody who buys oil, specs it for a fleet, or just has it poured in at a shop needs to understand what is changing before it shows up at the next service interval. This is not a marketing refresh or a new label on the same jug. It is a genuine category change, the kind the industry only goes through about once a decade. The last one landed in 2016. Before that, 2006. So if it feels like you have been buying the same oil forever, that is because, in category terms, you nearly have. What is coming in January is a real shift in how these oils are formulated, what they are certified to do, and in one important case, which engines they are even allowed to go into. If you sit on the leadership side of a carrier, this belongs on your radar now as a procurement, budgeting, and equipment-planning item rather than a shop-floor detail to delegate and forget. articles.content: China completes world's first commercial green ammonia ship-to-ship bunkering - Splash247 CMB.TECH China has completed the world’s first commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering operation, transferring 1,000 tonnes of the fuel to Belgian shipowner CMB.TECH’s newly delivered Mineral Europa. The operation, carried out on October 13 and 14 at an anchorage off Zhoushan, saw the dedicated bunkering vessel Shenghang Yongle supply the 210,000 dwt bulker, the world’s first ammonia-powered dry bulk carrier. The fuel was produced using renewable electricity at China Energy Engineering’s Songyuan green hydrogen and ammonia project in Jilin province, before being transported through Nanjing to Zhoushan. The operation brought together China Energy Engineering, CMB.TECH and Jiangsu Andefu Energy Technology, establishing a commercial supply chain stretching from renewable fuel production to delivery onboard an oceangoing vessel. “The offshore ship-to-ship bunkering model offers remarkable advantages,” said Li Jingguang, chairman of China Energy Engineering’s hydrogen division, noting that future transfers could reach 2,000 or even 3,000 tonnes. Chinese maritime authorities supervised the operation, implementing special safety measures to handle the highly toxic fuel. Mineral Europa, delivered earlier this month, is heading across the Pacific to Australia for commercial operations. CMB.TECH expects 21 ammonia-powered vessels to enter its fleet by 2029, including 18 bulkers. TagsCMB.TE

articles.content: What Daimler's Finance And Global Chiefs Revealed About Diesel, Driverless Trucks, And The Future Of The Industry - FreightWaves On a rainy Saturday morning in Charlotte, inside the brand new North American headquarters of Daimler Truck Financial Services, four of the company’s senior leaders traded the usual press-conference script for something closer to a fireside chat, and over the better part of an hour they said more about where this industry is actually heading, from the engine under your hood to the driver who may one day not be in the seat to the rising cost of borrowing money against a truck, than most carriers will hear in a year of official announcements. Kevin Bangston, president and CEO of Daimler Truck Financial Services USA LLC, handled the view from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Goetz Johanning, head of strategy and realization for the North American financial services arm, moderated. The session was set up as a conversation rather than a presentation, and the candor showed. REUTERS/Stringer EU Targets Major Russian Shipyards in Sweeping Sanctions Expansion Mike Schuler Total Views: 117 October 12, 2026 The European Union has imposed sanctions on some of Russia’s most important shipyards, including major submarine builders, naval ship-repair facilities and yards involved in commercial vessel construction, as part of a sweeping expansion of restrictions targeting the country’s military-industrial complex. The new sanctions, adopted Monday, add 826 Russian companies and 743 executives to the EU’s sanctions list. Sweden Releases Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker After Seven-Month Detention Mike Schuler Total Views: 318 October 12, 2026 Swedish authorities have cleared the sanctioned tanker Sea Owl 1 to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor, following confirmation that the vessel is now legitimately registered under the flag of Equatorial Guinea. The Swedish Transport Agency announced Monday that it had lifted an operating ban imposed on the tanker in March over irregularities involving its flag registration and documentation. The vessel has remained anchored off Trelleborg, on Sweden’s southern coast, since authorities boarded it on March 12 amid concerns over its seaworthiness and registration status. According to the Swedish Coast Guard, the tanker was initially found to be falsely flying the flag of Comoros. An attempt to reflag the vessel to Cameroon in May also proved invalid, leaving the ship effectively without a recognized flag state. articles.title: OOCL revenue up 45.1% on trans-Pacific surge
articles.summary:
OOCL saw higher revenue per container and increased cargo volumes across all four of its trade regions.
The post OOCL revenue up 45.1% on trans-Pacific surge appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: OOCL revenue up 45.1% on trans-Pacific surge - FreightWaves Orient Overseas Container Line reported a 45.1% year-over-year increase in third-quarter liner revenue to $3.28 billion, as higher revenue per container and increased cargo volumes drove gains across all four of its reported trade regions. OOCL handled 2.12 million twenty-foot equivalent units in the quarter ended Sept. 30, up 9% from a year earlier, according to an Oct. 9 operational update from parent Orient Overseas (International) Ltd., itself majority-owned by China’s Cosco Shipping Holdings. Average liner revenue per TEU increased 33.1%. Cargo growth outpaced a 3.6% increase in loadable capacity. articles.content: Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses - FreightWaves AI startup Evos raised $9 million in pre-seed funding to develop autonomous software operators for small and midsized industrial businesses, including freight brokerages, the company announced Wednesday. This comes as the company looks to automate routine work without requiring businesses to replace their existing software. The round was co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures, with participation from Crosslink Capital, Utopia Capital Management, Sandwith Ventures and angel investors. Evos said it surpassed $1 million in annual recurring revenue four weeks after launching. The company did not disclose its valuation or the number of customers using its platform. How it works Evos is developing AI operators that learn how employees make decisions and carry out specific business functions within a company’s existing systems. Rather than requiring employees to prompt an AI tool for every task, the operators are designed to manage an assigned function independently once their decisions consistently match those of experienced workers. The approach targets smaller industrial businesses where operational knowledge often rests with experienced employees rather than documented procedures. articles.content: Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up - FreightWaves Tesla had 103 job openings with Semi in the title posted at its Sparks, Nevada, truck plant as of Oct. 16, according to Tesla’s careers site. The listings come three weeks after the plant started high-volume Semi production on Sept. 24. The hiring is for a 1.7-million-square-foot factory designed to build 50,000 trucks a year, as fleets line up orders for a truck Tesla first showed in 2017. Tesla has not said how many Semis the plant is building now. Before the dedicated line opened, the Semi fleet numbered just under 200 pilot trucks, delivered to customers including DHL, PepsiCo and US Foods. Drayage carrier IMC Logistics ordered 50 Semis this month, following WattEV’s 370-truck order in May. Tesla was also named lead manufacturer on a 2,500-truck order through the ZET SCALE alliance in September, though the alliance did not say how many of those trucks will be Semis. Tesla CEO Elon Musk told analysts in July, “We have started production with the Tesla semi-truck.” The company’s second-quarter shareholder update said production was expected to begin later in the year. Semi openings span assembly to dispatch The Semi listings include quality technicians for stamping, body-in-white and powertrain; equipment maintenance technicians for general assembly and the drivetrain; and a CDL driver, a dispatcher and an endurance fleet driver. Several are night-shift roles, including a battery production supervisor

articles.content: Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels - FreightWaves United Parcel Service’s new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines is 15 times larger than its predecessor, enabling the express carrier to provide up to two days faster delivery for customers within Asia and improve connectivity across its global network. UPS (NYSE: UPS) spent $80 million on the expansion project, which includes specialized handling areas for healthcare, high-tech and manufacturing customers with time-sensitive and temperature-sensitive shipments. Parcel handling capacity increased to an average daily volume of 46,000, with maximum processing capacity of 15,000 pieces per hour, according to a news release on Thursday. The announcement marks the first time UPS has disclosed the size of the capital expenditure to expand its Clark hub, which now covers 323,000 square feet. UPS now operates 170 flight segments into and out of Clark every week, connecting businesses across Asia Pacific, India, Europe and the United States in as little as one business day. The new hub has also created nearly 600 jobs, the company said. In August, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the transfer of six UPS flying rights between Hong Kong and Warsaw, Poland, and Hanoi, Vietnam, to Clark Airport to support growing trade flows between the Philippines and Hong Kong. articles.content: West Africa's ore boom meets China's growing VLOC armada - Splash247 Winning West Africa is fast becoming dry bulk shipping’s biggest growth engine, with its mineral export boom poised to absorb the equivalent of another 120 capesizes by 2030. UK consultancy Tradeviews forecasts in a new report that shipments from the region will surge 50% from 2025 levels to 303m tonnes by the end of the decade, with Guinea’s giant Simandou iron ore project leading the charge. Crucially for shipowners, the long voyages to China will magnify the impact on vessel demand. “West Africa looks set to remain the fastest growing long-haul source of dry bulk cargo,” Tradeviews stated. The growth is already evident. The five West African exporters covered by the consultancy shipped 160.1m tonnes in their principal trades during the first eight months of this year, up 25% year on year. Liberian iron ore exports nearly doubled to 10.1m tonnes. Tradeviews expects regional exports to reach 267m tonnes next year, with Guinean iron ore shipments climbing to 45m tonnes in 2027 and approximately 112m tonnes by 2030. Bauxite exports, meanwhile, are forecast to retreat from a peak of nearly 194m tonnes this year to 153m tonnes by 2030 as Guinea pushes ahead with domestic alumina processing. A capesize round voyage between Guinea and China takes approximately 78 days, compared with just 29 days on the Australia-China route.
